mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or if the mechanism fails during a high-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY > 6%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1.5% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST) predicts weak consumer and capex demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -1.5% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if GDP and housing recover within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or if the unemployment rate reverts below 5% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months, accompanied by a fall in retail sales (RSAFS), indicates weakening manufacturing and demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if INDPRO rebounds within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month drop in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency easing in response to a financial shock, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls below 2% in one month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or if the rate does not remain below 2% for at least one additional month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in both housing starts (HOUST) and personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) YoY growth above 4% signals a robust demand recovery, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises for 2 consecutive months AND GDPC1 YoY > 4%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or if the housing or GDP growth reverts below trend within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals strong labor market expansion, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month +1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or if PAYEMS growth stalls below 0.5% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent divergence between rising CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY) and flat federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS unchanged for 3 months) signals monetary policy lag, which erodes real equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% for 3 months AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or if FEDFUNDS rises within the next month.
